Page.add_circle_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Circle(rect, color=..., interior_color=..., border=Border(...))) adds an ellipse with its appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_file_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(FileAttachment(point, data, filename=..., description=..., icon=AttachmentIcon.PUSH_PIN)) embeds a file behind an icon and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_freetext_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(FreeText(rect, text, size=..., text_color=Color(...), color=fill, align='left', rotate=..., callout=[...])) adds free text with its appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_highlight_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Highlight(quads)) adds a highlight and returns its Annotation; color is a Color and content becomes contents.

Page.add_ink_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Ink(handwriting, ...)) adds freehand strokes, a sequence of point sequences, with their appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_line_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(LineAnnotation(p1, p2, line_endings=(...), ...)) adds a line with its appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_polygon_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Polygon(points, ...)) adds a closed polygon with its appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_polyline_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(PolyLine(points, ...)) adds an open polyline with its appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_rect_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Square(rect, color=..., interior_color=..., border=Border(...))) adds a rectangle with its appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_redact_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Redaction(quads, fill=Color(...), overlay_text=..., text_color=..., align=...)) marks areas for removal; applying them is page.redact (Rewriting).
Page.add_redact_annot.note: pymupdf fills with white by default; Redaction fills with black unless fill= says otherwise.

Page.add_squiggly_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Squiggly(quads)) adds a squiggly underline with its appearance and returns its Annotation; color is a Color and content becomes contents.

Page.add_stamp_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Stamp(rect, icon=StampIcon.APPROVED, rotate=...)) adds a stamp with its appearance and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_strikeout_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(StrikeOut(quads)) adds a strikeout with its appearance and returns its Annotation; color is a Color and content becomes contents.

Page.add_text_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Note(point, contents=text, icon=NoteIcon.NOTE)) adds a note with its 20-point icon and returns its Annotation.

Page.add_underline_annot.hint: page.annotations.add(Underline(quads)) adds an underline with its appearance and returns its Annotation; color is a Color and content becomes contents.

Page.annots.hint: page.annotations lists Annotation handles other than links and widgets; filter on annotation.type instead of passing types.

Page.artbox.hint: Read page.boxes.art, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.bleedbox.hint: Read page.boxes.bleed, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.clip_to_rect.note: Removes page content outside a rectangle.

Page.cropbox.hint: Read page.boxes.crop, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.cropbox_position.hint: Read page.boxes.crop: its top-left corner is (crop.x0, crop.y1) in PDF user space.

Page.delete_annot.hint: del page.annotations[index] removes an annotation with its popup.

Page.delete_link.hint: del page.links[index] removes a link; its annotation goes at the next pruning save.

Page.derotation_matrix.hint: pylopdf reads and writes in display space with the rotation resolved; drop the step, and map display space to PDF user space with ~page.user_to_display.

Page.draw_bezier.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.bezier(p1, p2, p3, p4, stroke=...), or canvas.path(PathBuilder()...) for a closed or filled curve.

Page.draw_circle.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.circle(center, radius, fill=..., stroke=...); fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Page.draw_cont.note: pymupdf's internal bookkeeping; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Page.draw_curve.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.bezier(p1, c1, c2, p3) with the curve's control points, or build it with PathBuilder.curve_to.

Page.draw_line.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.line(p1, p2, stroke=...); fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Page.draw_oval.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.ellipse(rect, fill=..., stroke=...); draw the ellipse of a quad inside canvas.transform(matrix).

Page.draw_polyline.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.polygon(points, close=False, fill=..., stroke=...); fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Page.draw_quad.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.polygon((quad.ul, quad.ur, quad.lr, quad.ll), fill=..., stroke=...).

Page.draw_rect.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.rect(rect, radius=..., fill=..., stroke=...), whose radius is in points where pymupdf's is a fraction of the shorter side; fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Page.draw_sector.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.path(PathBuilder().sector(center, radius, start, sweep, pie=True), fill=..., stroke=...), with angles in degrees clockwise from the x axis.

Page.draw_squiggle.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.path(PathBuilder().wave(p1, p2, breadth=2), stroke=...).

Page.draw_zigzag.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.path(PathBuilder().zigzag(p1, p2, breadth=2), stroke=...).

Page.extend_textpage.note: Reading designs the API for reusable text pages.

Page.find_tables.hint: Use page.tables(strategy=..., clip=...), which returns a list of Table records; table.rows replaces extract().
Page.find_tables.note: pymupdf's tuning keywords, header detection, and to_pandas() come with Understanding.

Page.first_annot.hint: next(iter(page.annotations), None) is the first annotation; iterate page.annotations instead of following annot.next.

Page.first_link.hint: next(iter(page.links), None) is the first link; iterate page.links instead of following link.next.

Page.get_bboxlog.hint: Call page.content(); every item has a bbox and a kind, and its context lists the clips around it.

Page.get_cdrawings.hint: Read page.content().paths, whose segments, paints, and strokes are immutable values.

Page.get_displaylist.hint: Call page.content(), which returns the page's painted items as an immutable Content sequence.

Page.get_drawings.hint: Read page.content(text_runs=False, images=False).paths: Path records with segments, fill, fill_rule, stroke, and bbox, in paint order; a path with both a fill and a stroke is pymupdf's fs type, and each path's context holds what extended=True listed.
Page.get_drawings.note: A stroke merges with the fill before it only when it directly follows a fill of the same segments. seqno is an item's position in page.content(). Layer names wait for hayro to report marked-content properties.

Page.get_image_bbox.hint: Keep the items of page.content().images whose xref is the image's object number, and read their bbox and matrix.

Page.get_image_info.hint: Read page.content(text_runs=False, paths=False).images: Image records with xref, bbox, matrix (pymupdf's transform), width, height, bits, colorspace, components, mask, encoded_size, and resolution.
Page.get_image_info.note: hashes= has no counterpart yet. Image masks report xref 0, because hayro does not expose their streams.

Page.get_image_rects.hint: Keep the items of page.content().images whose xref is the image's object number, and read their bbox and matrix.

Page.get_images.hint: Read page.resources.images: ImageObject handles with xref, width, height, bits, colorspace, alternate_colorspace, filters, soft_mask, mask, and is_stencil, in place of tuples.
Page.get_images.note: Images that only annotation appearances list are not included, as in pymupdf. The resource name and the Form that lists an image are read from page.obj['Resources'] with the object model.

Page.get_links.hint: page.links lists Link handles: read link.rect and link.target instead of the 'from', 'uri', 'page', 'to', 'zoom', 'file', and 'name' keys.

Page.get_pixmap.hint: Use page.pixmap(dpi=...) or page.pixmap(matrix=...), not both; annots= is annotations=.
Page.get_pixmap.note: background= is an extension. Only scaling matrices are supported, and colorspace= takes gray or RGB; CMYK is not rendered.

Page.get_svg_image.hint: Use page.svg(), which draws text as paths at 72 dpi.
Page.get_svg_image.note: hayro-svg takes no transform and always draws text as paths, so matrix= and text_as_path=False have no counterpart.

Page.get_text.hint: Use page.text() for "text", page.words() for "words", page.layout().blocks for "blocks", and page.layout().to_dict() or page.layout(chars=True).to_dict() for "dict" and "rawdict".
Page.get_text.note: Reading adds the html, xhtml, xml, json, and rawjson outputs and clip=, flags=, and delimiters=.

Page.get_text_blocks.hint: Read page.layout().blocks, Block records with text, bbox, and lines.

Page.get_text_words.hint: Call page.words(), which returns Word records with text, bbox, block, line, and index.

Page.get_textpage.note: pylopdf caches each page's interpretation internally today.

Page.get_textpage_ocr.note: page.ocr() and page.apply_ocr() run pylopdf's own OCR today; Tesseract's language= and tessdata= will raise.

Page.get_texttrace.hint: Call page.content() and read the glyphs of its text_runs, each run with its font, size, paints, and graphics context.
Page.get_texttrace.note: Layer names and the font dictionary's object number wait for hayro to report marked-content properties and font identity.

Page.insert_image.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.image(rect, source, keep_aspect=..., rotate=...), with a path, encoded JPEG or PNG bytes, or a Pixmap as source in place of filename=, stream=, and pixmap=; an image drawn again is stored once, so xref= is not needed, and page.content().images reports each placement's xref.
Page.insert_image.note: Masks, alpha, image replacement, and layers come with Writing.

Page.insert_link.hint: page.links.add(rect, target), where target is a URI string, Destination(page, point, zoom), RemoteDestination(file, page), Launch(file), or NamedAction(name).

Page.insert_text.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.text(text, point, font=..., size=..., fill=Color(r, g, b)), with a Font from Font.standard(), Font.from_file(), or Font.installed(); it draws every line, line_height times size apart, and rotate= turns them clockwise about the point, so pymupdf's rotate=90 is rotate=270.

Page.insert_textbox.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.textbox(rect, text, font=..., size=..., align="left"), which returns a TextFit whose spare_height, like pymupdf's return value, is negative when nothing was drawn; Font.text_height(text, size, width=...) measures the height the text needs before drawing; rotate= turns the text clockwise inside the rectangle, so pymupdf's rotate=90 is rotate=270.

Page.language.note: ISO 32000 defines /Lang on the catalog, structure elements, and marked content, not on pages; decided with tagged structure in Understanding.

Page.last_point.hint: Build the path with a PathBuilder and read its current_point, the end of its last segment.

Page.links.hint: page.links is a sequence of Link handles: iterate it instead of calling it, and test the type of link.target instead of passing kinds.

Page.load_annot.hint: Find the annotation in page.annotations by its xref or name.

Page.load_links.hint: next(iter(page.links), None) is the first link; iterate page.links instead of following link.next.

Page.new_shape.hint: with page.draw() as canvas: draws paths and text in the order of the calls and writes them when the block ends, as Shape.commit() did.

Page.refresh.note: pylopdf pages always read the current document state, so the method will do nothing.

Page.repair_flat_rbgs.note: Rebuilds radio-button groups whose widgets share a name without a parent field.

Page.rotation_matrix.hint: pylopdf reads and writes in display space with the rotation resolved; drop the step, and map PDF user space with page.user_to_display.

Page.run.hint: Call page.content() for the items that the page paints; pylopdf has no device protocol.

Page.search_for.hint: Use page.search(text), which returns one Rect per match.
Page.search_for.note: clip= and quads= come with Reading.

Page.set_artbox.hint: Assign page.boxes.art = rect, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.set_bleedbox.hint: Assign page.boxes.bleed = rect, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.set_cropbox.hint: Assign page.boxes.crop = rect, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.set_language.note: ISO 32000 defines /Lang on the catalog, structure elements, and marked content, not on pages; decided with tagged structure in Understanding.

Page.set_mediabox.hint: Assign page.boxes.media = rect; as in pymupdf, the other boxes are removed.

Page.set_rotation.hint: Assign page.rotation = angle, a multiple of 90; another angle raises ValueError, where pymupdf sets 0.

Page.set_trimbox.hint: Assign page.boxes.trim = rect, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.show_pdf_page.hint: Inside with page.draw() as canvas:, call canvas.page(rect, docsrc.pages[pno], clip=..., keep_aspect=..., rotate=...), which draws the page as vectors, from any open document or this one; clip is in the source page's display coordinates, and rotate turns clockwise, so pymupdf's rotate=90 is rotate=270.

Page.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Page.thisown.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Page.transformation_matrix.hint: Use page.user_to_display, which maps PDF user space to display space with the rotation included; pymupdf's matrix stops before the rotation.

Page.trimbox.hint: Read page.boxes.trim, in PDF user space as stored, where pymupdf flips y against the top of the MediaBox.

Page.update_link.hint: Assign link.rect and link.target on a handle from page.links.

Page.widgets.note: doc.form covers fields until Interaction adds widget handles.

Annot.hint: page.annotations lists Annotation handles with type, rect, contents, author, subject, created, modified, name, icon, intent, color, interior_color, opacity, flags, xref, and page.

Annot.blendmode.hint: annotation.blend_mode is a BlendMode member, or None without /BM.

Annot.border.hint: annotation.border is a Border(width, style=BorderStyle..., dashes=...) record, or None when the annotation has none.

Annot.colors.hint: Read annotation.color and annotation.interior_color, Color records or None.

Annot.delete_responses.hint: for reply in annotation.replies: del page.annotations[page.annotations.index(reply)] removes the replies with their popups; del annotation.popup_rect removes the popup.

Annot.file_info.hint: annotation.file.filename, .description, and .size describe the embedded file; annotation.file is None for other annotations.

Annot.get_file.hint: annotation.file.read(max_size=...) returns the embedded file's data.

Annot.has_popup.hint: annotation.popup_rect is not None tells whether the annotation has a popup.

Annot.info.hint: Read annotation.contents, author, subject, created, modified, name, and icon.

Annot.irt_xref.hint: annotation.in_reply_to is the Annotation that this one replies to, or None; its xref is in_reply_to.xref.

Annot.is_open.hint: annotation.is_open tells whether the popup, or a note without one, opens when the page is shown.

Annot.line_ends.hint: annotation.line_endings is a (start, end) pair of LineEnding members, or None for an annotation other than a line or polyline.

Annot.next.hint: Iterate page.annotations instead of following annot.next.

Annot.parent.hint: annotation.page is the page that holds the annotation.

Annot.popup_rect.hint: annotation.popup_rect is the popup's display Rect, or None without a popup.

Annot.popup_xref.hint: annotation.obj['Popup'] is the popup annotation's dictionary.

Annot.rotation.hint: annotation.rotation is the clockwise turn of the content as the page is displayed: the page's rotation less /Rotate, which annotation.obj holds.

Annot.set_irt_xref.hint: Assign annotation.in_reply_to = other_annotation, or None, to set or remove /IRT.

Annot.set_popup.hint: Assign annotation.popup_rect = rect to add or move the popup; del annotation.popup_rect removes it.

Annot.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Annot.thisown.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Annot.type.hint: annotation.type is an AnnotationType member; annotation.obj['Subtype'] holds the name and annotation.intent the intent.

Annot.update.hint: pylopdf applies annotation changes immediately; remove the update() call.

Annot.update_file.hint: annotation.file.write(data) replaces the embedded file's data; its name and description stay.
Annot.update_file.note: Renaming the file or changing its description goes through annotation.obj['FS'] in the object model.

Annot.vertices.hint: annotation.vertices lists the display Points of a line, polygon, or polyline; an ink annotation's points are annotation.strokes, one tuple of Points per stroke.

Widget.note: Field handles in doc.form cover fields until Interaction adds widget handles.

Widget.choice_values.hint: Read doc.form[name].choices, FieldChoice records with value and label.
Widget.choice_values.note: Widget handles in page.widgets come with Interaction.

Widget.field_flags.note: Widget handles in page.widgets come with Interaction.

Widget.field_name.hint: Read doc.form[name].name, or iterate over the keys of doc.form.
Widget.field_name.note: Widget handles in page.widgets come with Interaction.

Widget.field_type.note: Widget handles in page.widgets come with Interaction.

Widget.field_type_string.hint: Read doc.form[name].type, a FieldType member whose value is a lowercase name such as text.
Widget.field_type_string.note: Widget handles in page.widgets come with Interaction.

Widget.field_value.hint: Read or assign doc.form[name].value; assignment regenerates the appearances at once, so no update() follows.
Widget.field_value.note: Widget handles in page.widgets come with Interaction.

Widget.text_font.note: doc.form.font draws filled values with a loaded OpenType Font today.

Widget.update.hint: pylopdf applies widget changes immediately; remove the update() call.

Link.border.hint: Read or assign link.obj["Border"] or link.obj["BS"], the annotation's border entries.

Link.colors.hint: Read or assign link.obj["C"], the annotation's border colour.

Link.dest.hint: link.target is a URI string, Destination(page, point, zoom), RemoteDestination(file, page), Launch(file), or NamedAction(name), or None for an action that pylopdf does not read.

Link.flags.hint: Read or assign link.obj["F"], the annotation flags.

Link.is_external.hint: isinstance(link.target, (str, RemoteDestination, Launch)) tells whether a link leaves the document.

Link.next.hint: Iterate page.links instead of following link.next.

Link.page.hint: link.target.page is the zero-based page of a Destination; link.page is the page that holds the link.

Link.parent.hint: link.page is the page that holds the link.

Link.set_border.hint: Read or assign link.obj["Border"] or link.obj["BS"], the annotation's border entries.

Link.set_colors.hint: Read or assign link.obj["C"], the annotation's border colour.

Link.set_flags.hint: Read or assign link.obj["F"], the annotation flags.

Link.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Link.thisown.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Link.uri.hint: link.target is the URI string of a URI link.

Outline.hint: pymupdf's Outline is one item; pylopdf's is OutlineItem, and pylopdf's Outline is the sequence that doc.outline returns.

Outline.dest.hint: Read item.destination: a Destination, RemoteDestination, Launch, NamedAction, URI string, or None.

Outline.destination.hint: Read item.destination; a named destination reads as the Destination it names.

Outline.down.hint: Read item.children, the item's children in order.

Outline.is_external.hint: Test item.destination: a RemoteDestination, a Launch, or a URI string leads outside the document.

Outline.is_open.hint: Read or assign item.is_open on the OutlineItem; assigning recounts the outline.

Outline.next.hint: Iterate over doc.outline or the parent's item.children; doc.outline.walk() visits every item.

Outline.page.hint: Read item.page: zero-based, and None for a target outside the document, where pymupdf returns -1.

Outline.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Outline.title.hint: Read or assign item.title on the OutlineItem.

Outline.uri.hint: Read item.destination: a URI target reads as its string.

Outline.x.hint: Read item.destination.point.x of a Destination with a point.

Outline.y.hint: Read item.destination.point.y of a Destination with a point.

Pixmap.note: page.pixmap() and ImageObject.to_pixmap() produce Pixmaps, and Pixmap.from_array() builds one from a uint8 array; pymupdf's other constructors are not provided.

Pixmap.pdfocr_save.hint: Insert the image into a page and run page.apply_ocr().

Pixmap.pdfocr_tobytes.hint: Insert the image into a page and run page.apply_ocr().

Pixmap.samples.hint: bytes(pix) copies the pixels; memoryview(pix) and numpy.asarray(pix) read them without a copy, shaped (height, width, channels).

Pixmap.samples_ptr.note: Raw memory address of MuPDF's sample buffer; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Pixmap.save.hint: output= is format= ('png' or 'jpeg') and jpg_quality= is quality=.
Pixmap.save.note: Writes PNG and JPEG; other formats belong to Pillow.

Pixmap.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Pixmap.tobytes.hint: Use pix.to_bytes('png') or pix.to_bytes('jpeg', quality=...); other formats belong to Pillow.

Pixmap.warp.hint: Warp the pixels with OpenCV on numpy.asarray(pixmap).

TextPage.note: Reading designs the API for reusable text pages; page.layout() returns the blocks, lines, spans, and characters as records today.

TextPage.poolsize.note: Size of MuPDF's text memory pool; it has no PDF-level meaning.

TextPage.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

TextPage.thisown.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Shape.hint: page.draw() returns a Canvas, a context manager that draws paths, text, images, and pages in the order of the calls and writes them as one Form XObject when its with block ends.

Shape.commit.hint: The canvas's with block writes the drawing when it ends; page.draw(underlay=True) writes it below the page's content.

Shape.doc.hint: Keep the page you called draw() on and read page.document.

Shape.draw_bezier.hint: canvas.bezier(p1, p2, p3, p4, stroke=...), or canvas.path(PathBuilder()...) for a closed or filled curve.

Shape.draw_circle.hint: canvas.circle(center, radius, fill=..., stroke=...); fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Shape.draw_cont.note: Raw content buffer of pymupdf's Shape; the canvas composes its content itself.

Shape.draw_curve.hint: canvas.bezier(p1, c1, c2, p3) with the curve's control points, or build it with PathBuilder.curve_to.

Shape.draw_line.hint: canvas.line(p1, p2, stroke=...); fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Shape.draw_oval.hint: canvas.ellipse(rect, fill=..., stroke=...); draw the ellipse of a quad inside canvas.transform(matrix).

Shape.draw_polyline.hint: canvas.polygon(points, close=False, fill=..., stroke=...); fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Shape.draw_quad.hint: canvas.polygon((quad.ul, quad.ur, quad.lr, quad.ll), fill=..., stroke=...).

Shape.draw_rect.hint: canvas.rect(rect, radius=..., fill=..., stroke=...), whose radius is in points where pymupdf's is a fraction of the shorter side; fill=Color(r, g, b) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(r, g, b), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) replace color, fill, width, lineCap, lineJoin, and dashes, and a Color's alpha the opacities.

Shape.draw_sector.hint: canvas.path(PathBuilder().sector(center, radius, start, sweep, pie=True), fill=..., stroke=...), with angles in degrees clockwise from the x axis.

Shape.finish.hint: Pass fill=Color(...) and stroke=Stroke(paint=Color(...), width=..., cap=..., join=..., dashes=...) to each canvas call; fill_rule=FillRule.EVEN_ODD replaces even_odd, and PathBuilder.close() closes a path.

Shape.height.note: The canvas draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; page.rect gives the drawing area.

Shape.horizontal_angle.hint: Use math.atan2(p.y - c.y, p.x - c.x), the angle from the x axis in display space.

Shape.insert_text.hint: canvas.text(text, at, font=..., size=..., fill=...) draws lines in call order with the paths, not on top of them; rotate= turns clockwise, where pymupdf turns anticlockwise.

Shape.insert_textbox.hint: canvas.textbox(rect, text, font=..., size=..., align=...) returns a TextFit; Font.text_height measures the height the text needs, and rotate= turns clockwise, where pymupdf turns anticlockwise.

Shape.ipctm.note: The canvas draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; page.rect gives the drawing area.

Shape.last_point.hint: PathBuilder.current_point is the end of the last segment added.

Shape.page.hint: Keep the page you called draw() on.

Shape.pctm.note: The canvas draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; page.rect gives the drawing area.

Shape.rect.hint: Union the rectangles you draw, or read the bbox of the page's content().paths after the canvas is written.

Shape.text_cont.note: Raw content buffer of pymupdf's Shape; the canvas composes its content itself.

Shape.totalcont.note: Raw content buffer of pymupdf's Shape; the canvas composes its content itself.

Shape.updateRect.hint: Union the rectangles you draw with the | operator of Rect.

Shape.width.note: The canvas draws in display coordinates, where these values of pymupdf's unrotated space would mix coordinate spaces; page.rect gives the drawing area.

Font.note: Font.standard(name) takes the 14 PostScript names, Font.from_file(path) and Font.from_bytes(data) load an OpenType face, with weight= selecting an instance of a variable face, and Font.installed(language=..., family=...) selects the face of an installed font extra; the codemod rewrites Font(...) calls. script=, ordering=, embed=, and pymupdf's other built-in fonts are not available.

Font.ascender.note: What FreeType reads for MuPDF: the OS/2 typographic ascender when the face sets USE_TYPO_METRICS and the hhea ascender otherwise, or the bounding box of MuPDF's URW font for a Standard 14 font; the canvas places lines of text with it.

Font.descender.note: From the same table as Font.ascender; the canvas places lines of text with it.

Font.has_glyph.note: Takes a one-character string and returns whether the face has a glyph for it, where pymupdf takes a code point and returns the glyph number; the codemod rewrites ord(c) and integer arguments. language=, script=, fallback=, and small_caps= are not available.

Font.is_serif.note: Classified from the PANOSE serif style or the family name, where pymupdf reports every OpenType face as serif.

Font.name.note: The family and style of an OpenType face, or the PostScript name of a Standard 14 font.

Font.text_length.hint: font.text_width(text, size) measures one line with the shaping that drawing uses; size has no default, and a line break raises.

Font.this.note: Handle of pymupdf's MuPDF binding; it has no PDF-level meaning.

Point.note: Immutable NamedTuple with finite coordinates, geometric operators, and tuple indexing, equality, and hashing.

Point.__setitem__.hint: Point values are immutable; build a new Point instead.

Point.transform.hint: Use p * m, which returns a new Point.

Rect.note: Immutable NamedTuple with finite coordinates, pymupdf's geometric operators, and tuple indexing, equality, and hashing.

Rect.__setitem__.hint: Rect values are immutable; build a new Rect instead.

Rect.include_point.hint: Use r | p, which returns a new Rect.

Rect.include_rect.hint: Use r | other, which returns a new Rect.

Rect.intersect.hint: Use r & other, which returns a new Rect.

Rect.normalize.hint: Use r.normalized(), which returns a new Rect.
Rect.normalize.note: No operator normalizes a rectangle, so the replacement needs a name.

Rect.transform.hint: Use r * m, which returns a new Rect.

IRect.note: Immutable NamedTuple of integers; fractional edges round outward.

IRect.__setitem__.hint: IRect values are immutable; build a new IRect instead.

IRect.include_point.hint: Use r | p, which returns a new IRect.
IRect.include_point.note: pymupdf's IRect version already returns a new IRect.

IRect.include_rect.hint: Use r | other, which returns a new IRect.
IRect.include_rect.note: pymupdf's IRect version already returns a new IRect.

IRect.intersect.hint: Use r & other, which returns a new IRect.

IRect.normalize.hint: Use r.normalized(), which returns a new IRect.
IRect.normalize.note: No operator normalizes a rectangle, so the replacement needs a name.

IRect.transform.hint: Use r * m, which returns a new IRect.

Quad.__setitem__.hint: Quad values are immutable; build a new Quad instead.

Quad.transform.hint: Use q * m, which returns a new Quad.

Matrix.note: Immutable NamedTuple with finite coordinates, geometric operators, and tuple indexing, equality, and hashing.

Matrix.__setitem__.hint: Matrix values are immutable; build a new Matrix instead.

Matrix.concat.hint: Use one * two, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.prerotate.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(deg) * m, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.prescale.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(sx, sy) * m, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.preshear.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(h, v, 1) * m, which returns a new Matrix.

Matrix.pretranslate.hint: Use pylopdf.Matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, tx, ty) * m, which returns a new Matrix.
